title: Professional tax: who levies it in each State
description: Which States and Union territories levy the tax on professions, trades, callings and employments on salary and wage earners, and under which Act, from 1 April 2026: one row for each whose instrument was read, with the words that levy the tax, the Act's extent where it leaves part of the State out or reaches beyond it, and its definition of salary or income verbatim, even where it cites the Income-tax Act, 1961; “…” marks words the ERP's copy leaves out. Where an official text says the State levies none, its row says so in that text's words: Odisha's Act repealed from 1 April 2026, Jammu and Kashmir's certificate, and Tamil Nadu's Act of 1992 repealed, its councils levying the tax instead, which the ERP does not hold. A State without a row is one whose text the ERP has not read, which says nothing of whether it levies the tax. The tax period is the month or year the tax is for, and the set answers for its first day.

cells.name: Punjab levies it as the State Development Tax under its Act of 2018
cells.law: The Punjab State Development Tax Act, 2018 (Punjab Act No. 11 of 2018)
cells.words: Subject to the provisions of Article 276 of the Constitution of India and provisions of this Act, there shall be levied and collected a tax on professions, trades, callings and employments.
cells.extent: It extends to the whole of the State of Punjab, and offices of the Government of Punjab and offices of any body, whether incorporated or not, which is owned or controlled by the State of Punjab situated in the capital of Punjab.
cells.salary: “salary” or “wage” includes pay or wages, dearness allowance and all other remunerations received by any person on regular basis, whether payable in cash or kind, and also includes perquisites and profits in lieu of salary as defined in section 17 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, but does not include any form of bonus or gratuity; Explanation.- Regular basis means a period exceeding one hundred and eighty days.

cells.name: Karnataka levies it under its Act of 1976
cells.law: The Karnataka Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1976 (Karnataka Act 35 of 1976)
cells.words: There shall be levied and collected a tax on professions, trades, callings and employment for the benefit of the State.
cells.salary: ‘salary’ or ‘wage’ includes pay or wage, dearness allowance and all other remunerations received or receivable by any person including any amount received by way of arrears of salary or bonus by whatever name called whether payable in cash or kind and also includes perquisites and profits in lieu of salary as defined in section 17 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Explanation.- (i) Where ‘bonus’ by whatever name called is received in part or full, then such bonus shall be spread over for twelve months of the year or to such number of months the bonus relates for purposes of computation of ‘Salary’ or ‘Wage’ for such months. (ii) Where arrears of salary is received in part or full, then such arrears shall be spread over for the relevant months for which it relates for purposes of computation of ‘Salary’ or ‘Wage’ for such months.
